Chapter One: Discovering the Power of Stillness in a Noisy World
Have you ever stopped to notice just how much noise we live with every single day? There’s the steady hum of traffic outside, those constant pings from your phone, and even the background chatter from the TV or radio that never really goes away. All of it blends together, creating a constant current of sound that’s easy to ignore—until you can’t.
And honestly, it’s not just the sounds around us. Inside, our minds are often even busier. Thoughts race, worries stack up, and it’s like your brain’s jumping from one thing to the next without a break. In a world like this, the idea of finding stillness can feel almost strange—or even a little uncomfortable. But here’s the thing: if you’ve ever had a taste of real quiet, you know there’s something special waiting in that silence. Something we might not even realize we’re missing.
Let me share a story. There was someone who, after a long day juggling work and family life, would sometimes just sit in her car in the driveway. No engine running, no plans, just… breathing. She wasn’t praying out loud or trying to figure out her next move. She was simply letting the noise settle. And in those small pauses, she felt a gentle shift—a softening, almost like being held by something bigger than her own thoughts. It wasn’t dramatic, but it was real. With time, she realized these moments weren’t empty—they were actually full of presence.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we crave that kind of stillness until we accidentally stumble into it. We’re taught that being productive and always moving means we’re living a meaningful life. But the deeper truth? Our souls need space to breathe. When your mind finally quiets—even if it’s just for a few minutes—you start to notice a different kind of awareness. It’s like your heart tunes in to a frequency that’s always been there, just waiting beneath all the noise.
That’s really where the journey into contemplative living begins. Not with grand gestures or complicated rituals, but with something so simple: just stopping. For some, it starts with a quiet walk early in the morning, when the world is still asleep and the air feels brand new. For others, it’s the hush that settles after a child finally drifts off to sleep, or the peaceful moment when you’re alone in your favorite chair. In those moments, the presence of God doesn’t show up with fireworks. It comes quietly—like a gentle invitation you might miss if you’re not paying attention.
The first step? Honestly, it’s often the hardest. Making room for silence can feel awkward, even a little unsettling. You sit there, and suddenly your mind throws up a pile of to-do lists and worries. But if you stick with it, that discomfort starts to fade. What’s left is a sense of being met—a quiet assurance you’re not alone in the silence. People who practice this over time say the quiet stops feeling empty and starts feeling deeply connected.
There’s another story I love. A man, after years of trying to “do” his faith perfectly, finally just let himself sit in silence every morning. At first, all he felt was impatience—like, “Is this really doing anything?” But slowly, he noticed he was less reactive during the day, more patient with his family, and more tuned in to little moments of beauty. He couldn’t really explain it, but he knew something sacred was happening in that stillness.
And that’s really the heart of contemplative practice. It’s about learning to be present, to listen, and to trust that God is already near. The world might always be noisy, but in those quiet spaces we carve out, a deeper presence is waiting. It isn’t about running away from life, but about meeting it—with open hands, and a quiet heart.
